results.name: corpus decks open in the real UI with every slide in the rail and the file's content drawn: shapes.pptx (6 slides, preset shapes + text), table_test.pptx (a table with its cell text), bar-chart.pptx (chart drawn from its cache as SVG), backgrounds.pptx

edit → save → python-pptx: retype the title by double-click, bold one word through the toolbar, add speaker notes, duplicate and hide a slide, insert a text box, drag a shape — the saved file carries exactly those edits, validates, and untouched parts keep their bytes
slide show: Present opens a full-window show at the first visible slide; → / Space / click advance, ← goes back, HIDDEN slides are skipped, Escape ends and returns to the editor

modal-shortcut failure test: with a shape selected, Delete / Backspace / Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+D pressed while the Save-as dialog, the slide show or the notes field has the keyboard never delete the shape, undo, or duplicate a slide; the same keys on the canvas do
legacy .fdeck outline opens as a real PowerPoint deck (titles, bullets, notes) and Save writes a .pptx that python-pptx reads
no page errors in any Slides session
